newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 17.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish health minister Michael Noonan will speak on the HIV blood controversy in parliament today but is expected to resist pressure to disband the Blood Transfusion Service Board.
- A long-awaited freedom of information bill will not come into effect for a year after its passage through parliament, Eithne Fitzgerald, the minister who proposed the legisation, said.
- The weekend agreement on an EU stability pact has driven Irish bond prices strongly ahead, leading to a fall in long-term interest rates.

- Airplanes Group, the investment vehicle set up by GPA as part of a refinancing, stands to lose cashflow of $7.3 million over the six months to next March because of a restructuring plan being proposed by Canadian Airlines.
- The strength of the Irish pound against other European currencies is creating problems for the Irish dairy industry, Noel Cawley, head of the Irish Dairy Board, said. IRISH INDEPENDENT
- A powerful group representing 20,000 members of the defence forces and police has warned it will not accept the new national pay deal.
- British prime minister John Major's dependency on the Ulster Unionists is beyond doubt following the first Commons test since the Conservatives lost their overall majority last week.
- A survey of company liquidations in Ireland has found worrying data on the absence of timely financial and management information, the Institute of Chartered Accountants said.
- Irish dairy manufacturers are facing serious losses on important European markets because the continuing strength of the Irish pound is making exports uncompetitive.
